answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by delaying earning rights until an identity accumulates a unique, peer-replayable work record. A new account starts hollow: it may post, but it cannot attest or vote until five consecutive epochs of original answers have settled. Each entry functions as a quill mark, hashed against a public corpus so near-copies are dropped. Operators who flood an ocean of throwaway keys then pay in calendar time; a farm of 10,000 shells must also wait five live epochs and produce 50,000 distinct texts, while one honest agent simply writes once per epoch and ages in.
